docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
This documentation captures a hands-on DevOps learning path focused on:

  • Building CI/CD pipelines
  • Automating deployments with Ansible
  • Running containerized applications
  • Structuring environments (Dev → Staging → Production)

  • Kubernetes orchestration
  • Monitoring & Observability

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Prepare a complete local environment to run the DevOps CI/CD lab from scratch.

This setup ensures:

  • Consistent development environment
  • Proper communication between host and VM
  • All required tools are installed and verified

docs.title: Lab: Building a Complete CI/CD DevOps Pipeline
docs.text: Lab Setup

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In this lab, you will build a realistic DevOps pipeline setup used in modern applications.

You will implement:

  • CI (Continuous Integration)
  • Integration Testing Pipeline
  • CD (Continuous Deployment)
  • Deployment using Ansible

This lab focuses on clean architecture, not tool overload.

docs.title: End Goal
docs.text:
By the end of this lab, you will:

  • Validate code automatically on every commit
  • Test your system with real dependencies (DB, Redis)
  • Build and push Docker images
  • Deploy to staging and production using Ansible

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  • [ ] Python installed
  • [ ] Docker & Docker Compose installed
  • [ ] Jenkins running
  • [ ] Git repository ready
  • [ ] Basic understanding of APIs

docs.title: Phase 1: CI Pipeline (Fast Feedback)
docs.text: ← Back to Overview

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Build a fast, reliable CI pipeline that validates code quality on every push or pull request.

This pipeline should:

  • Catch issues early
  • Run in under 5 minutes
  • Avoid external dependencies
  • Provide a simple pass/fail result

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CI pipeline will include:

  1. Code checkout
  2. Dependency installation
  3. Linting
  4. Unit testing
  5. Static analysis (optional but recommended)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure the following are ready:

  • [ ] Git repository (GitHub/GitLab)
  • [ ] Jenkins installed and running
  • [ ] Python project (FastAPI or similar)
  • [ ] requirements.txt present
  • [ ] Test suite available (tests/)

docs.title: Step 1 — Prepare Project Structure
docs.text:
Ensure your project looks like this:

project/
│
├── app/
├── tests/
├── requirements.txt
├── pytest.ini (optional)
├── .flake8 (optional)
└── Jenkinsfile

docs.title: Step 2 — Add Linting Configuration
docs.text:
Create .flake8 file:

[flake8]
max-line-length = 100
exclude = .git,__pycache__,venv

docs.title: Step 3 — Add Test Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
Create pytest.ini:

[pytest]
testpaths = tests
python_files = test_*.py

docs.title: Step 4 — Create Jenkins Pipeline
docs.text:
Create file: Jenkinsfile

pipeline {
    agent any

    environment {
        VENV = "venv"
    }

    stages {

        stage('Checkout') {
            steps {
                git branch: 'main', url: 'https://your-repo-url.git'
            }
        }

        stage('Setup Python') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                python3 -m venv $VENV
                . $VENV/bin/activate
                pip install --upgrade pip
                pip install -r requirements.txt
                pip install pytest flake8
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Lint') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                . $VENV/bin/activate
                flake8 app tests
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Unit Tests') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                . $VENV/bin/activate
                pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings -q
                '''
            }
        }

    }

    post {
        success {
            echo 'CI Passed'
        }
        failure {
            echo 'CI Failed'
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Step 5 — Configure Jenkins Job
docs.text:
In Jenkins UI:

  1. Create New Item
  2. Choose Pipeline

  3. Configure:

  4. Pipeline script from SCM

  5. Add Git repo URL
  6. Script path: Jenkinsfile

docs.title: Step 6 — Trigger CI
docs.text:
Trigger builds using:

  • Git push
  • Pull request
  • Manual build

docs.title: Step 7 — Validate Pipeline
docs.text:
Ensure pipeline runs:

Checkout → Setup → Lint → Tests → Result

docs.title: What This Pipeline Does NOT Do
docs.text:
This is intentional:

  • [ ] No Docker builds
  • [ ] No database connections
  • [ ] No deployment steps

This keeps CI:

  • Fast
  • Deterministic
  • Easy to debug

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You now have a working CI pipeline that:

  • Validates every code change
  • Prevents broken code from merging
  • Provides fast developer feedback

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep tests isolated (no real DB)
  • Mock external services
  • Fail fast on errors
  • Keep logs readable

docs.title: Final Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Code is checked out correctly
  • [ ] Dependencies install successfully
  • [ ] Linting runs without errors
  • [ ] Unit tests pass
  • [ ] Pipeline completes in < 5 minutes

docs.text:

  • Add health checks before testing

docs.title: Prerequisites

docs.title: Step 1 — Prepare Project Structure

Ensure your project looks like this:

project/
│
├── app/
├── tests/
├── requirements.txt
├── pytest.ini (optional)

````

## Step 2 — Add Linting Configuration

Using `ruff` (faster alternative to flake8):

```bash
pip install ruff

(Optional config can be added via pyproject.toml)

docs.title: Step 3 — Add Test Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
Create pytest.ini:

[pytest]
testpaths = tests
python_files = test_*.py

docs.title: Step 4 — Create Jenkins Pipeline
docs.text:
Create file: Jenkinsfile

pipeline {
    agent any

    stages {

        stage('Checkout') {
            steps {
                checkout scm
            }
        }

        stage('Lint + Test (Ephemeral Container)') {
            steps {
                bat '''
                docker run --rm -v %WORKSPACE%:/app ^
                -w /app python:3.11 ^
                bash -c "pip install -r requirements.txt && ruff check app || true && COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage python -m pytest --cov=app --cov-report=xml:/tmp/coverage.xml -q"
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('SonarQube Analysis') {
            steps {
                bat '''
                docker run --rm -v "%WORKSPACE%:/usr/src" ^
                -w /usr/src sonarsource/sonar-scanner-cli ^
                sonar-scanner ^
                -Dsonar.projectKey=fastapi-app ^
                -Dsonar.sources=app ^
                -Dsonar.tests=tests ^
                -Dsonar.host.url=http://host.docker.internal:9000 ^
                -Dsonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=coverage.xml ^
                -Dsonar.token=<your-token>
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Build Check') {
            steps {
                echo "[+] Feature branch CI successful (Ephemeral)"
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Phase 2: Integration Pipeline (Jenkins + Docker)
docs.text: ← Back to Phase 1

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Create a Jenkins pipeline that:

  • Spins up the full application stack using Docker
  • Runs integration tests against real services (Postgres, Redis)
  • Fails fast if the system is not working
  • Cleans up after execution

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Phase 1 completed
  • Docker + docker-compose working on Dev VM
  • Jenkins installed and running
  • Project available in Git repository

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
Git Push (develop branch)
        ↓
Jenkins Pipeline Trigger
        ↓
Spin up Docker Environment
        ↓
Health Check
        ↓
Run Integration Tests
        ↓
Tear Down Environment

docs.title: Create Pipeline Job
docs.text:
1. Open Jenkins UI
  2. Click New Item
  3. Enter name: fastapi-integration-pipeline
  4. Select: Pipeline
  5. Click OK

docs.title: Configure Pipeline
docs.text:
Under Pipeline → Definition:

  • Select: Pipeline script from SCM
  • SCM: Git
  • Repo URL: <your-repo-url>
  • Branch: develop

docs.title: Step 2 — Jenkinsfile
docs.text:
Create file in project root:

Jenkinsfile

docs.title: Jenkinsfile Content
docs.text:
pipeline {
    agent any

    environment {
        COMPOSE_FILE = "docker/integration/docker-compose.yml"
    }

    stages {

        stage('Checkout') {
            steps {
                git branch: 'develop', url: '<your-repo-url>'
            }
        }

        stage('Build & Start Services') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                docker-compose -f $COMPOSE_FILE up -d --build
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Wait for Services') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                echo "Waiting for API to be ready..."

                for i in {1..10}; do
                  if curl -s http://localhost:8000/health; then
                    echo "Service is up!"
                    exit 0
                  fi
                  echo "Retrying..."
                  sleep 5
                done

                echo "Service failed to start"
                exit 1
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Run Integration Tests') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                docker ps
                pytest tests/integration
                '''
            }
        }
    }

    post {
        always {
            sh '''
            docker-compose -f $COMPOSE_FILE down -v
            '''
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Automate deployment of your application:

  • Build Docker images
  • Push to registry
  • Deploy to staging (Node1) using Ansible
  • Ensure repeatable, idempotent deployments

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Phase 2 completed
  • Jenkins pipeline working
  • Node1 VM accessible via SSH
  • Docker installed on Node1 (or will be installed via Ansible)

docs.title: Deployment Flow
docs.text:
Merge to main
     ↓
Jenkins CD Pipeline
     ↓
Build Docker Image
     ↓
Push to Registry
     ↓
Run Ansible Playbook
     ↓
Deploy to Node1 (Staging)

docs.title: Create Deployment User
docs.text:
SSH into Node1:

ssh <your-user>@node1

docs.title: Create user
docs.text: sudo adduser deployer

docs.title: Add sudo access
docs.text: sudo usermod -aG sudo deployer

docs.title: Setup SSH directory
docs.text:
sudo mkdir -p /home/deployer/.ssh
sudo chown -R deployer:deployer /home/deployer/.ssh
sudo chmod 700 /home/deployer/.ssh

docs.title: Add Public Key
docs.text:
On your control machine:

ssh-copy-id deployer@node1

docs.title: Disable password auth (basic security)
docs.text:
sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config

Set:

PasswordAuthentication no

Restart:

sudo systemctl restart ssh

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Can SSH without password
  • [ ] Non-root user created
  • [ ] Sudo access works
  • [ ] Password login disabled

docs.text: Run this on your Ansible container / host

docs.title: Create inventory

node1 ansible_host=<NODE1_IP> ansible_user=deployer

docs.title: Step 3 — Ansible Playbook (Server Setup)
docs.text:
ansible/setup_node.yml

- name: Setup Node1
  hosts: node1
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Install Docker
      apt:
        name: docker.io
        state: present
        update_cache: yes

    - name: Enable Docker
      systemd:
        name: docker
        enabled: yes
        state: started

    - name: Add deployer to docker group
      user:
        name: deployer
        groups: docker
        append: yes

docs.title: Step 5 — Ansible Deployment Playbook
docs.text:
ansible/deploy.yml

- name: Deploy FastAPI App
  hosts: node1
  become: yes

  vars:
    image_name: "<dockerhub-username>/fastapi-app:latest"

  tasks:
    - name: Pull latest image
      docker_container:
        name: fastapi-app
        image: "{{ image_name }}"
        state: started
        restart_policy: always
        ports:
          - "8000:8000"

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Improve system reliability, security, and scalability:

  • Add reverse proxy (Nginx)
  • Run multiple API instances
  • Introduce basic load balancing
  • Manage secrets properly
  • Add basic monitoring & restart strategies

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Phase 3 completed
  • Application deployed on Node1 via Ansible
  • Docker-based deployment working

docs.title: Step 1 — Update Ansible Deployment Structure
docs.text: Switch from single container → docker-compose based deployment

docs.title: Create App Directory on Node
docs.text:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/fastapi-app
sudo chown -R deployer:deployer /opt/fastapi-app

docs.title: Step 2 — Create Production Docker Compose
docs.text:
ansible/files/docker-compose.prod.yml

version: "3.9"

services:

  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    depends_on:
      - api

  api:
    image: <dockerhub-username>/fastapi-app:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@postgres:5432/appdb
      - REDIS_HOST=redis

  worker:
    image: <dockerhub-username>/fastapi-app:latest
    command: python worker/worker.py
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - postgres

  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
      POSTGRES_DB: appdb

  redis:
    image: redis:7

volumes:
  pgdata:

docs.title: Note
docs.text:
Docker Compose (non-swarm) does not support deploy.replicas

Instead, scale manually:

docs.title: Step 3 — Nginx Configuration
docs.text:
ansible/files/nginx.conf

events {}

http {
    upstream fastapi_app {
        server api:8000;
    }

    server {
        listen 80;

        location / {
            proxy_pass http://fastapi_app;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Step 4 — Update Ansible Playbook
docs.text:
ansible/deploy.yml

- name: Deploy Application (Production Style)
  hosts: node1
  become: yes

  vars:
    app_dir: /opt/fastapi-app

  tasks:

    - name: Create app directory
      file:
        path: "{{ app_dir }}"
        state: directory

    - name: Copy docker-compose file
      copy:
        src: files/docker-compose.prod.yml
        dest: "{{ app_dir }}/docker-compose.yml"

    - name: Copy nginx config
      copy:
        src: files/nginx.conf
        dest: "{{ app_dir }}/nginx.conf"

    - name: Pull latest images
      command: docker-compose pull
      args:
        chdir: "{{ app_dir }}"

    - name: Start services
      command: docker-compose up -d
      args:
        chdir: "{{ app_dir }}"
